lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Yolanda, this is Pierre. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hey, yeah, I was waiting for your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So did you manage to finish eating by 7 on 3 nights?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I did it 1 days, then the weekend happened.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I get so hungry at night, I can't sleep if I don't eat something.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I told my family I'm done eating at 8.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: The research is very clear, you have to eat earlier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, but you don't know my schedule.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Nights are the hard part.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Work has been crazy, I'm doing overtime.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Work took over this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My family eats late, like at 9, and I'm not going to eat alone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Eating together matters to you, maybe even more than the goal.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've always eaten late, that's how we do it at home.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that work keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Finishing dinner a little earlier, like by 7, makes the 13 hours a lot easier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Black coffee, tea or water are fine during the fast. They don't break it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, we had a birthday party, there was so much food.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Lots of celebrations this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the overnight fast fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you eat breakfast every day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe finish eating by 7:30 on 5 nights?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 7.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll ask my son to come with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: work made this week harder, you still got 1 days in, and your plan is to finish eating by 7:30 on 5 nights. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Yolanda, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

tags.note: Reports one day met; some effort
Values feeling better when sticking to plan; coach did not reflect
Pushes research claim, no permission asked
Reframes as caring, not lack of commitment
Motivation: lower blood sugar; enjoys fasting
Plans phone alarm as a step
Plans support from son for barrier

flags.reason: Coach asserts 'the research is very clear, you have to eat earlier' without permission, triggering pushback at line 14.
Participant's 'I feel better about myself when I stick to it' was not reflected; coach moved to a family question.
'I need to get my sugar down' is a strong health reason; coach replied 'It's completely your call' without exploring it.

score.summary: Yolanda's plan is concrete and she rated her confidence at 7/10, with barriers identified and a summary and next contact set. Coaching was mixed: the persuasive 'research is very clear' line and missed change talk about her blood sugar and self-image reduced the partnership.
strengths: Line 19 and 21: complex reflections named that eating together matters and reframed the issue as work, not lack of caring.
Line 35: complex reflection captured her openness while wanting a plan that fits real life.
Line 50: asked about barriers and line 52 summarized the plan clearly.
coaching_tips: Line 13: replace the persuasive research claim with permission, e.g., 'Would it be okay to share what the research says about timing?'
Line 12 and 28: reflect the change talk ('Feeling better about yourself matters to you' / 'Lowering your sugar is a big reason'), then ask what that would look like.
Line 27 and 29: pair 'It's completely your call' with a curious question to deepen her own reasons rather than closing the topic.
